newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Thursday on weak sentiment, traders said.
The key Jauary 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,225 yuan ($388) per tonne, rising 36 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,190.
March did not trade, May fell 90 to 3,260, July 50 to 3,350, September 10 to 3,380 and November 10 to 3,390.
Combined volume fell to 8,600 tonnes from 12,600.
Traders said weak market sentiment pushed most contracts down except January.
"Speculative buying supported the January contract," one trader said.
"But there was no follow-up buying of most contracts due to poor fundamentals," he added.
Analysts expect soybean to move in a narrow range in the next few days in the absence of market-moving news.
